examples.name: Default
examples.summary: The Threats vs requests chart: allowed requests as an area, blocked and logged threats as lines. Each series means a state, so it wears a status color. Hover, or focus the plot and use the arrow keys, to read every series at one point.

examples.name: Forms
examples.summary: The same three series as lines, as areas and as grouped bars. Lines and areas share a point scale; any bar switches the category axis to bands so every mark sits on a band center.

examples.name: Stacked
examples.summary: Parts of a total over time. Stacked bars keep a 2px surface gap between segments and round only the top of each column.

examples.name: MultiSeries
examples.summary: Eight hosts. The first six take the six series slots in order and the last two fold into Other, so no hue is ever generated or reused. Toggle a host in the legend: the others keep their colors.

examples.name: Horizontal
examples.summary: Ordered horizontal bars with the value at each bar end, the form for a top-N list. One series means one color for every bar; bar length already carries the magnitude.

examples.name: Loading
examples.summary: A Skeleton fills the plot while the first response loads.

examples.name: Empty
examples.summary: No series has a value, so the plot renders an EmptyState at full plot height and the dashboard keeps its rhythm. Name the reason in the copy: nothing in the range, filters that match nothing (offer Clear filters), or a source that is not set up yet (offer the setup action).

examples.name: ErrorState
examples.summary: The request failed. A danger Alert takes the plot; the card around it keeps its title and controls.

examples.name: Refetching
examples.summary: A new range is loading. The previous render holds at reduced opacity instead of flashing a skeleton.

examples.name: TableView
examples.summary: The accessible twin of the chart, made visible: every label by every series. It is always present for assistive tech.
